problem: History-aware VLN agents (HAMT, DUET, VLN-CE BERT) are computationally heavy because the visual encoder processes all 36 panorama views at every step. Existing input-adaptive inference (MuE early-exit) assumes independent inputs and, applied to VLN, gives negligible savings with large performance loss.
motivation: About 99.5% of FLOPs are spent in the visual encoder, and this matters for resource-constrained robots. VLN inputs have spatial locality (navigable views and their neighbours matter most) and temporal locality (consecutive panoramas overlap), which one-size-fits-all early exit ignores.
key_idea: Process only navigable views plus k neighbouring views, exit early with rank-dependent adaptive thresholds, and reuse cached view embeddings via SimHash LSH, all exploiting the spatio-temporal locality of VLN.
insight: Naive MuE fails because ViT layer-to-layer cosine similarity peaks at layers 7-8 and then decreases, so it exits before the activations have saturated; per-step FLOPs fall 7% but the agent takes more steps, so total FLOPs rise. Masking all non-navigable views costs 33% SR, while adding k neighbours recovers most of it (R2R, k=1..6: SR 54.3->62.8 vs 66.2 base). LSH caching is nearly lossless but saves little alone; combined with k-extension it adds 2-24% savings. Failures under corruption appear to be recognition failures (the agent fails to stop), not navigation failures.
method: k-extension (spatial): keep the navigable views and k neighbouring views on each side, and zero-mask the other views so the ViT skips them (k=4-6 gives about 50% savings).

Rank-based adaptive early-exit thresholds: apply MuE with budgeted-batch inference so each view exits at its own layer; threshold T=T0*exp(-A*R), where R is the index distance to the nearest navigable view (T0=1.0, A=9e-4), and navigable views are fully processed.

Temporal caching with SimHash LSH: random hyperplanes (n=10 bits) hash raw views into buckets; an embedding is reused if cosine similarity exceeds 0.85 (discrete) or 0.95 (continuous); navigable views are never cached.
Scan-only subgoal generation module for continuous VLN: a U-Net predicts navigable views from laser occupancy scans alone, before image encoding, so only about 5 of 36 views are encoded.
Combined pipeline (Algorithm 1): per view, fully encode if navigable; else if within k, use cache or run MuE with a rank threshold; else output a zero vector.

setting.backbone: HAMT (ViT-B/16 + BERT), DUET (ViT-B/16 + BERT + object features), VLN-CE BERT (ResNet-152 + BERT); pretrained off-the-shelf agents, no retraining except the scan-only SGM U-Net
setting.training_data: Original agent checkpoints are reused; only the scan-only SGM is trained on Matterport3D scene data following Krantz et al.
setting.observation: Panoramic RGB (36 views, 224x224 in discrete; 3x480x640 in Habitat) plus laser occupancy scans for the continuous SGM
setting.action_space: Discrete nav-graph viewpoints (HAMT, DUET); low-level forward/turn actions with predicted waypoints (VLN-CE)
setting.privileged: Navigable views from the nav graph in discrete settings (part of the standard agent action space); none in continuous, where the scan-only SGM predicts them

numbers_note: Efficiency numbers are GFLOPs per navigation, not in the standard metric set. The R2R-CE base row is SR 43.23, SPL 36.53, GFLOPs 18074.05. The paper does not print a separate 'Ours' HAMT row with k-extension alone on R2R in the main text; those variants are in the appendix ablations.
results: Across 7 benchmarks and 3 agents, the method cuts GFLOPs by about 56% on average in standard VLN with about an 11.7% SR drop (R2R HAMT: 4763->1918 GFLOPs, SR 66.16->60.41). In continuous R2R-CE it saves about 87% of GFLOPs with an 8% SR drop, and 90% with LSH. It far outperforms MuE, which loses 42-56% SR for only 21-25% savings.
limitations: Substantial SR loss of 10-20% in standard VLN, and the method is markedly less robust to visual corruptions (12-31% loss vs 5-21% for the base agent); the agent tends to overshoot the target.
Evaluated only in simulation, and on REVERIE/SOON the object-feature extraction cost is treated as a constant; wall-time savings (about 40%) are smaller than the GFLOPs savings (about 60%).
Requires navigable views known in advance (nav graph or scan-only SGM); k must be tuned per benchmark; early exit is not usable with ResNet encoders.
